memories.memory: I work as a policy implementation officer for the city council and am currently competing for a permanent senior role that would raise my salary by about €6,000 a year.
Last October, I challenged my department head over a rushed €38,000 software procurement because I thought the evaluation process was too weak, and our relationship has been tense ever since.
I am still in occasional contact with my former partner, Elena, even though we ended our two-year relationship in February after she became frustrated with how often I prioritized late work meetings.
My younger brother lent me €2,400 in June to cover moving costs, and I have been repaying him €200 each month.
A colleague named Tomas helped me prepare for the senior-role interview, and I would feel personally responsible if management blamed him for sharing internal project information with me.
I turned down a three-month secondment in Brussels last year because it would have delayed my promotion locally, although I sometimes regret missing the opportunity.
I took four days of sick leave in November after several weeks of poor sleep and headaches during an audit, but I returned before my doctor recommended because I did not want to look unreliable.
